## 1. Electric Vehicle

**Title:** Electric Vehicle

**Slug:** `electric-vehicle` (auto-generated, but verify)

**Meta box fields:**
- Short code: `EV`
- Clock hours: `72`
- Weeks: `10`
- Tuition: `12000`
- SOC code: `11-3021`
- Accent: Blue
- Tagline: `Vehicle architecture, battery systems, powertrain, and ISO 26262 functional safety.`

**Body content (paste into the editor):**

```
This program provides students with the opportunity to understand electric vehicle architecture and domain functionalities. The program covers automotive development history, market trends, automotive standards, and design fundamentals. Students learn the systematic design of vehicle domains including body, battery, chassis, powertrain, thermal, infotainment, and telematics at the system, sub-system, and component levels. Industrial design topics include system engineering, safety engineering, quality control, and supply chain management. Tools covered include PREEvision, Vector tools, MATLAB, LabVIEW, ANSYS, and Maxwell 3D.

## What you'll learn

- Comprehensively understand the key systems of an electric vehicle
- Understand electric vehicle codes and standards
- Fully understand in-vehicle networking fundamentals
- Understand the key aspects for E/E architecture design and development
- Understand the functionalities and functional exchange between systems
- Design and integrate core systems of an electric vehicle
- Apply industrial design knowledge to automotive design

## Curriculum

**Module 1 — General introduction to electric vehicle (Week 1).** Automotive industry history, present situation of EV development, power electronics theory and devices.

**Module 2 — Automotive fundamentals (Weeks 1–3).** E/E architecture, battery cell chemistry, in-vehicle network protocols, ISO 26262 functional safety, ISO/SAE 21434 cybersecurity.

**Module 3 — EV system design (Weeks 4–6).** Body, powertrain, battery, chassis, charging, thermal, and power distribution systems. Overview of ADAS, autonomous driving, OTA, and infotainment.

**Module 4 — Automotive tools (Week 7).** PREEvision, CANalyzer, CANoe, MATLAB Simulink, LabVIEW.

**Module 5 — Industrial design (Week 8).** System engineering, safety engineering, integration, validation, and troubleshooting.

**Module 6 — Common skills training (Week 9).** Presentation, leadership, teamwork, project management.

**Module 7 — Capstone project (Weeks 8–10).** Design and validate a subsystem for an electric vehicle. Includes design documentation, ECU integration, harness work, test cases, and root-cause analysis.

## Graduation requirements

To complete this program, students must finish all prescribed portions and earn the equivalent of a B grade plus a passing rubric on participation and the capstone project. A final exam is required.
```

## 2. Autonomous Driving

**Title:** Autonomous Driving

**Slug:** `autonomous-driving`

**Meta box fields:**
- Short code: `AV`
- Clock hours: `96`
- Weeks: `10`
- Tuition: `12000`
- SOC code: `11-3021`
- Accent: Red
- Tagline: `Computer vision, deep learning for AV, robotic operating systems, and motion planning.`

**Body content:**

```
This program prepares students for engineering positions in the autonomous driving industry. The curriculum covers fundamentals of autonomous vehicle architecture, image processing and recognition systems, robotic operating systems with localization and navigation components, and practical AI tools used in industry. Students complete a capstone subsystem design project on a test bench or lab car.

## What you'll learn

- Completely understand key components of an autonomous driving car
- Understand the key tools to design and test an autonomous driving car
- Understand deep learning and reinforcement learning
- Understand planning and navigation algorithms for autonomous driving
- Understand the structure and function of the intelligent system of an autonomous driving car
- Be able to design the core system of an autonomous driving car

## Curriculum

**Module 1 — General introduction to autonomous driving (Week 1).** Vehicle structure, ADAS/AD system architecture, functional safety, simulation via CarSim or CarMaker.

**Module 2 — Image processing and recognition system (Weeks 2–4).** Computer vision algorithms, deep learning theory, CNN, object detection, domain adaptation.

**Module 3 — Robotic operating system of autonomous driving (Weeks 4–6).** Localization, operating system, deep reinforcement learning, GNSS, safety considerations.

**Module 4 — Practical AI tools for autonomous driving (Weeks 7–8).** HD Map implementation, deep learning perception models, motion planning algorithms, statistical tools.

**Module 5 — Industrial design (Week 9).** System engineering, safety engineering, integration, validation, troubleshooting.

**Module 6 — Common skills training (Week 9).** Presentation, leadership, teamwork, project management.

**Module 7 — Capstone project (Weeks 8–10).** Design and validate a subsystem for an autonomous driving car. Includes test bench setup, integration, and per-test-case troubleshooting.

## Graduation requirements

Complete all modules and earn the equivalent of a B grade plus a passing rubric on participation and the capstone project. A final exam is required.
```

## 3. Machine Learning & Artificial Intelligence

**Title:** Machine Learning & AI

**Slug:** `machine-learning-ai`

**Meta box fields:**
- Short code: `ML/AI`
- Clock hours: `88`
- Weeks: `10`
- Tuition: `8500`
- SOC code: `11-3021`
- Accent: Blue
- Tagline: `Probability, statistics, deep learning, NLP, and computer vision with PyTorch and TensorFlow.`

**Body content:**

```
This program provides a foundation in artificial intelligence both theoretically and practically. Students learn probability theory, statistics, machine learning, and deep learning, then choose one specialty area: natural language processing, speech recognition, or computer vision. The capstone project applies the chosen specialty to a real-world problem.

## What you'll learn

- Comprehensively understand the mathematical foundation of AI
- Understand the concept of different learning algorithms
- Proficiently apply AI techniques to real-world problems
- Earn one specialty and project experience in the AI field

## Curriculum

**Module 1 — Algebra and statistics (Weeks 1–2).** Linear algebra, probability theory, random variables, statistical inference, Bayesian statistics.

**Module 2 — Data structures and algorithms (Weeks 3–5).** Python, software design principles, deep learning frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch), algorithm analysis, data structures.

**Module 3 — Machine learning (Weeks 5–7).** Supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, deep learning architectures (CNN, RNN, LSTM), regularization techniques.

**Module 4 — AI applications (Weeks 8–9).** Natural language processing (word embedding, RNN, Transformer) and computer vision (image classification, object detection, segmentation).

**Module 5 — Common skills training (Week 10).** Presentation, leadership, teamwork, project management.

**Module 6 — Capstone project (Weeks 8–10).** Pick a specialty (theoretical, NLP, or computer vision) and apply ML/DL to a real-world problem. Optionally integrate with hardware or a user interface.

## Graduation requirements

Complete all modules and earn the equivalent of a B grade plus a passing rubric on participation and the capstone project. A final exam is required.
```

## 4. Advanced Robotics

**Title:** Advanced Robotics

**Slug:** `advanced-robotics`

**Meta box fields:**
- Short code: `ROBOTICS`
- Clock hours: `96`
- Weeks: `10`
- Tuition: `8000`
- SOC code: `11-3021`
- Accent: Red
- Tagline: `Robotic operating systems, perception, deep reinforcement learning, and motion planning.`

**Body content:**

```
This program introduces fundamentals and advanced technologies of robotics: system design, sensing and perception, decision-making, motion planning and trajectory generation, robot control, concurrency, and real-time systems. The interdisciplinary curriculum covers electronics, mechatronics, physics, automation and control theory, computer vision, and artificial intelligence. Students gain hands-on experience with industrial robots and aerial robots, completing a capstone subsystem design on a real platform.

## What you'll learn

- Understand the concepts in robotics and automation
- Apply problem-oriented sensing and actuation system design
- Understand sensing fusion methods and conventional robot control strategies
- Navigate the entire pipeline using robots to solve real-world applications
- Understand robot skill learning techniques and implementation methods
- Understand prevalent industrial robots

## Curriculum

**Module 1 — Image processing and recognition system (Weeks 1–3).** Computer vision algorithms, deep learning theory, CNN, object detection, domain adaptation.

**Module 2 — Robotic operating system (Weeks 3–5).** Robotic OS design, perception, control, planning, deep reinforcement learning algorithms.

**Module 3 — Practical robotics (Weeks 6–8).** Visual perception model development, motion planning, control systems, statistical techniques in robotic development.

**Module 4 — Industrial design (Week 9).** System engineering, safety engineering, integration, validation, troubleshooting.

**Module 5 — Common skills training (Week 9).** Presentation, leadership, teamwork, project management.

**Module 6 — Capstone project (Weeks 8–10).** Design and validate a subsystem for a real operating robotic system. Modify and test perception, control, or planning components.

## Graduation requirements

Complete all modules and earn the equivalent of a B grade plus a passing rubric on participation and the capstone project. A final exam is required.
```
